open.guidance:
Preserve each assertion's conditions, uncertainty, attribution, scope and negation in that assertion's own phrase, participants, value and native qualifiers. When splitting a sentence, carry each governing condition to every assertion it qualifies; a separate statement or an intact quote does not replace that association. Preserve the actual actor and the bearer of each attribute. Resolve a pronoun only from explicit source context; do not treat a page heading as the physical bearer merely because it introduces the text. Do not drop governed negatives or turn absence of evidence into a negative fact. Keep the native output schema and preserve source wording where required.
Illustrative abstract examples only; do not add their participants or facts to the actual passage.
Source: "Agent A chooses option B while condition C remains unknown."
Correct statement: ["Agent A chooses option B while condition C remains unknown.", "Agent A", "chooses", "option B", null, {"while":"condition C remains unknown"}, null, null].
The same statement with no governing condition is incorrect; a separate unknown-state statement does not repair it.
Source: "Plan P requires a check confirming condition C."
Correct statements include ["Plan P requires a check confirming condition C.", "Plan P", "requires", "a check", null, null, null, null] and ["Plan P requires a check confirming condition C.", "a check", "confirming", "condition C", null, {"mood":"requires"}, null, null].
The confirming statement without inherited required modality is incorrect: the source does not say that the check happened or confirmed C. Inherited modality applies only to the assertions governed by it. Preserve the source's complete requirements; do not omit their content to avoid unsupported claims. Keep every referenced participant in e and keep the native schema.
Preserve the enclosing referent of a status or judgment. A status of a proposal, request, plan, claim or report does not automatically apply to a resource, method or person mentioned inside it. Keep that described referent under its source wording in e; a Markdown link target is not a replacement for the bearer of the status.
Abstract example: "Group G has not approved A's conditional request to use resource B." Correct: Group G —has not approved→ A's conditional request to use resource B. Wrong: Group G —has not approved→ resource B. List the described request as an entity; do not shorten it to the embedded resource.
Abstract table example: with columns Item | Description and row Request R | Resource B under condition C; not an approved plan, the non-approved-plan status belongs to Request R, not Resource B. Wrong: Resource B —is not→ an approved plan. Preserve the complete description and the condition on the content it actually governs using the native table rules. These examples establish no facts or extra types for the actual input.
Preserve the bearer established by table headers and section context. In a navigation/index table whose first column identifies a page/document, a link label naming an object does not make that physical object the bearer of page coverage. Use the literal linked document path written in the passage as the page/document entity; do not normalize or invent a path. Attach the table's coverage/content to that document. Do not equate a document and its subject or alias them as the same entity. Abstract example: Page | Coverage; [Object A](entities/object-a.md) | History and observations: subject entities/object-a.md (kind document), phrase Coverage, value History and observations; not physical Object A as bearer. This does not change object-valued domain tables. These examples establish no facts for the actual passage.
When splitting narrative content in a table cell, preserve governing attribution and event context established by its row and headers. Carry the speaker/reporting person into each claim attributed to that person, including multiple clauses within that same explicitly attributed table cell; do not turn that person into the physical actor or bearer of the reported proposition. Carry the row's explicit event into observations or actions scoped to that event. Do not invent attribution or events or repeat context unrelated to the claim. Abstract example: Speaker | Statement; Person Q | Process P does not guarantee outcome O. Extract Process P —does not guarantee→ outcome O with qualifier says: Person Q, not an unqualified claim. Abstract example: Event | Account; Event E | Person Q used method M on sample S. Extract Person Q —used→ method M with qualifiers on: sample S and event: Event E. These examples establish no facts for the actual passage; preserve native output and source wording.
An explicit speaker column governs the contents of its attributed cell. Outside that context, a semicolon by itself does not extend a reporting verb to a separate independent prose clause. Preserve continued attribution when the text explicitly establishes it, but do not invent it from punctuation alone. Abstract prose: Person Q says proposition P; event E occurred. The occurrence of E is not attributed to Q unless the passage explicitly makes it part of Q's report. Keep genuine table and prose attribution; these examples establish no input facts.
Distinguish the time of an asserted relation from the time or condition of an action mentioned inside that assertion. Set ended only when the source explicitly states cessation of that asserted relation. An earlier position, later evidence, or the time of a proposed action does not itself establish cessation. Preserve a temporal restriction on a referenced action in its phrase or native qualifiers; do not turn it into an end time of the surrounding reporting, evaluation or recommendation. Retain genuine explicit start and end times on the assertions they actually govern. Do not infer retraction from changed circumstances.

phrase.guidance:
Preserve the exact assertion, its participant roles, attribution, uncertainty and scope. Do not rewrite subject, object or literal to make a property fit. Negation must survive in the selected property meaning or in the complete literal value itself; a negative verb with an affirmative literal does not become a positive has_property assertion. A fully negative literal state can be retained with an appropriate attribute only if the subject is its actual bearer. Absence of reporting is not proof of nonoccurrence; unknown is not false. Direction reversal is not negation. Use the supplied definitions rather than property names alone. A relation between entities cannot bind a literal-valued attribute, and vice versa.
Choose only supplied per-item candidates. If no candidate expresses the assertion with the supplied participants and value, return null. A conservative null is preferable to changing the meaning. Keep the upstream response format and all expected item IDs.
Check the actual subject and endpoint against the property roles: the subject of a text attribute must be the bearer of that exact value, not merely an entity mentioned by it. A broader entailed property is allowed by the native contract when it preserves these participants and the asserted meaning. Do not replace a reporting or evidential relation with generic possession when the predicate or value loses that distinction.

proposal.guidance:
Preserve the exact assertion, its participant roles, attribution, uncertainty and scope. Do not rewrite subject, object or literal to make a property fit. Negation must survive in the selected property meaning or in the complete literal value itself; a negative verb with an affirmative literal does not become a positive has_property assertion. A fully negative literal state can be retained with an appropriate attribute only if the subject is its actual bearer. Absence of reporting is not proof of nonoccurrence; unknown is not false. Direction reversal is not negation. Use the supplied definitions rather than property names alone. A relation between entities cannot bind a literal-valued attribute, and vice versa.
Recommend an existing property only when both its meaning and relation/attribute shape fit the unchanged signature. Do not send a literal to a relation just because its name sounds appropriate. Proposals must obey all upstream support and competency-question rules; do not invent supporting shapes. An item may remain unresolved when neither valid reuse nor a justified proposal exists. Do not interpret fewer proposals as an objective overriding meaning.
Preserve reporting modality: a reported action is not an unqualified action by its reporter. Preserve who reports and who acts in the definition and supported signature; do not recommend an unconditional action property when that changes the assertion.
Illustrative abstract examples; use only the current operation's schema and supplied candidates, not the example names as additional types.
1. Entity A has literal "feature B": a compatible positive attribute may fit. Entity A lacks literal "feature B": the same positive attribute is wrong; preserve the negation with an eligible negative meaning, or leave unresolved. Do not invent a polarity field or edit the literal.
2. Source A records literal "action B did not occur": an attribute can preserve the complete negative content if its definition fits the source and value. This differs from a negative verb with affirmative literal "action B".
3. Source A does not mention action B: this does not establish that action B never occurred. Source A and the actor of B are different participants.
4. Actor A performs action B on entity C: C is not interchangeable with a claim about C. Preserve the actual subject and endpoint; do not substitute a participant from the surrounding quotation.
5. A text-valued signature cannot reuse an entity-to-entity relation. Only proposal may propose a warranted attribute under the native support rules; otherwise leave unresolved.
6. Evidence supports but does not conclusively establish claim B is not equivalent to evidence offers no support. A type conflating source omission with nonperformance needs clarification. A genuine synonym with matching definition and roles can reuse the existing type. These examples do not preassign decisions for the actual input.
